Subject: RFP items — Implementation & canary questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the RFP response so far. Procurement forwarded a few technical questions that the architecture team wants addressed before we move to the commercial review. We're targeting a pilot start the week of Jan 10, 2027 and need to validate the following so we can finalize the MAP. Please see the attached questionnaire (Bluebridge_RFP_questionnaire.xlsx). High level asks: 

- Support for on-prem HSM / enterprise KMS: do you support customer-managed keys for private deployments (VPC/on-prem)?
- Model version pinning and automatic fallback: how will Redwood handle model rollbacks during canary failures?
- Data residency and audit logs: retention windows and availability of request-level audit logs for compliance reviews.
- Integration surface: eventing (Kafka/Confluent), auth (SAML/OAuth2), and database connectors (JDBC/SQL).
- Canary gating: recommended ramp percentages, metric thresholds (latency, error rate, quality-regressions), and minimum observation windows.
- Pre-warm / KV cache strategy for cold-starts: suggested warm-up steps to reduce p95 spikes.

Can you send a draft implementation timeline, recommended canary gating matrix, and an initial responsibilities table (Bluebridge vs Redwood)? Also confirm any required network access (IP ranges, firewall rules) and a contact for your security/infra lead.

Appreciate a reply by EOD Tuesday (Nov 30) so we can include it in our internal scoring.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Senior Procurement Manager
Bluebridge Financial

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our draft integration checklist and a first-pass MAP (both marked v0.3). High-level responses inline below and in the attached runbook.

Quick answers:
- On-prem KMS/HSM: supported for Redwood Private. We integrate with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS connectors; HSM-based signing supported for key material used to encrypt caches and logs.
- Model pinning & rollback: you can pin a model version per route. For canaries we recommend an automatic rollback policy on either (a) sustained latency degradation > 20% vs baseline or (b) error-rate increase > 2x above baseline, or (c) quality regression flagged by your test prompts.
- Audit logs: request-level audit with immutable retention (configurable 30/90/365 days) and exportable in NDJSON for SIEM ingestion.
- Connectors: native Kafka output + webhook + JDBC sync helpers. For data flow we propose a staging topic and a pre-processor lambda for schema enforcement.
- Canary gating: see attached \"canary_matrix\" tab in integration_matrix_v2.xlsx. Short summary: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 48–72 hour windows with auto-rollback guardrails.
- KV cache warm-up: we recommend an automated prefix prefill job during the staging to minimize p95 spikes; instructions in runbook.

Open items for Bluebridge:
1) Security contact for key exchange and firewall rule approval.
2) Confirmation of staging dataset for quality regression checks.
3) Clarify whether private deployment (dedicated GPUs in your VPC) or hosted dedicated pool is preferred.

Next steps: if it looks good I suggest a 30-minute call with our solutions team (Sean) and Marissa from platform engineering to confirm the canary thresholds and staging access. I can schedule Wed or Thu this week UTC-friendly.

Thanks,

Naomi Feldman

Naomi / team — quick tech summary and actions. See attached runbook (redwood_runbook_v1.pdf) and updated integration matrix (integration_matrix_v2.xlsx). Key points below: 

1) Deployment model & KMS:
- For on-prem HSM: Redwood Private supports KMIP and direct HSM integration for key wrap/unwrap. We'll require an outbound TLS tunnel to our control-plane endpoints for orchestration; data plane can remain in-customer VPC.
- For hosted dedicated: we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integration; logs encrypted at rest.

2) Canary plan (recommended):
- Stage A (staging): Sanity + quality run against staging dataset (48 hours).
- Stage B (canary): Traffic routing 1% (24h) -> 5% (24h) -> 20% (48h) -> 50% (48h). Metric thresholds (example): p50 latency <= baseline + 15%, p95 <= baseline + 40%, error-rate <= baseline * 1.5, quality regression <= 1% failure on golden prompts.
- Auto-rollback triggers: sustained breach of any threshold over observation window or majority vote on eval suite.
- Manual gates: after 20% and 50% steps we recommend a manual review cadence with a short sign-off window (4 hours).

3) Autoscaling & capacity:
- Use dedicated GPU pool with min/max nodes: 2 -> 12 for pilot. Autoscale policy tied to queue depth and p95 latency.
- Pre-provisioned burst capacity available for initial ramp.

4) KV cache & warm-up:
- Provide prefix prefill task during staging that populates the KV cache for top 10k prefixes. This reduces cold-start p95 spikes.
- Instrument cache hit-rate dashboards in Console and add alerts for <70% hit-rate during early ramps.

5) Integration specifics:
- Kafka: use staging topic redwood.bluebridge.staging; we provide a connector template.
- Auth: support for SAML 2.0 and service account JWTs for automation.
- DB writes: JDBC sink for logging outputs into your warehouse (redacted columns per contract).

6) Rollout responsibilities (short):
- Bluebridge: provide staging dataset, firewall rules, security contact, and signed MAP.
- Redwood: provide runbook, connectivity guidance, automation for prefill, and on-call support during canary.

Estimated timeline (pilot target Jan 10):
- Week of Dec 6: security & network approvals; staging cluster created.
- Week of Dec 13: runbook review + prefill dry run.
- Week of Dec 20: end-to-end smoke + quality checks.
- Week of Jan 3: final cutover rehearsal.
- Week of Jan 10: pilot go-live.

Open items for ops: network CIDR list (I'll attach in a follow-up) and confirmation on whether they want automatic rollback to a variant model or to frozen previous version.

Subject: Bluebridge MAP & Canary guardrails — request for sign-off

Emily / Samir — attaching the consolidated MAP and runbook (v0.3) following our internal review. Summary of milestones and deliverables below; please review and sign via the DocuSign link included if this aligns with Bluebridge timelines.

Milestones (high level):
- Network & security approvals (Bluebridge) — target Dec 10
- Staging cluster provisioned (Redwood) — target Dec 13
- Prefill + staging quality runs (joint) — target Dec 20
- Rehearsal & smoke (joint) — target Jan 3
- Pilot go-live (1% traffic) — target Jan 10

Canary guardrails (short):
- Ramp: 1% (24h) -> 5% (24h) -> 20% (48h) -> 50% (48h)
- Automatic rollback triggers: p95 > baseline + 40% sustained over step window; error-rate > 2x baseline sustained; golden-prompt quality regression > 1%
- Manual sign-off: required at 20% and 50% steps; 4-hour review window recommended

Responsibilities:
- Bluebridge: staging dataset, firewall rules, security contact, sign-off on quality checks
- Redwood: provisioning, runbook, prefill automation, monitoring dashboards, on-call during ramps

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: higher than expected cold-start p95 spikes. Mitigation: KV prefill and short traffic drip with alerting.
- Risk: schema mismatch between webhook consumer and your downstream. Mitigation: staging schema enforcement job and contract tests.

Attachments (final): MAP_Bluebridge_Redwood_v0.3.docx; redwood_runbook_v1.pdf; integration_matrix_v2.xlsx

Sign here: https://docusign.com/en/link/BB-RB-MAP-2026-11

If you can sign by Dec 7 we'll lock the staging dates and begin provisioning. Happy to meet for a 30-minute alignment call Thu (Nov 30) or Mon (Dec 4) — let me know which works.
